benchmark_points.bp1: Markov_Functional_CCY_Model.pdf p.14 says that in the single-currency model the drift could be chosen freely.
benchmark_points.bp2: In the cross-currency model, the freedom to choose the drift freely is gone.
benchmark_points.bp3: For a given FX functional, a corresponding drift is needed for the model to remain arbitrage-free.
benchmark_points.bp4: Insisting on a specific drift, such as zero, would fix all FX functional forms through the no-arbitrage relation (22).
benchmark_points.bp5: crosscurrencymfm.pdf p.6 says the functional form of FX_{T_i} must satisfy equation (19), the forward-FX/expectation identity.
benchmark_points.bp6: Fixing mu_{i-1} in advance would, in general, produce an FX_{T_i} that fails equation (19) when calibrating to digital swap options.
benchmark_points.bp7: crosscurrencymfm.pdf p.7 says mu_{i-1} is F_{T_{i-1}}-measurable.
benchmark_points.bp8: The Brownian increment is independent of F_{T_{i-1}}.
benchmark_points.bp9: The drift must be measurable with respect to sigma(FX_{T_{i-1},T_i}).
benchmark_points.bp10: The drift is therefore a function of the forward FX rate.
benchmark_points.bp11: Markov_Functional_CCY_Model.pdf p.10 says that in a discrete model a change of numeraire via an adapted drift change is generally only an approximation.
benchmark_points.bp12: The Girsanov mean-shift argument does not hold exactly over a discrete step.
benchmark_points.bp13: Design A is described in crosscurrencymfm.pdf.
benchmark_points.bp14: Design A uses the domestic spot measure.
benchmark_points.bp15: Design A is after Fries and Rott.
benchmark_points.bp16: In Design A, the drift is written as mu_{i-1}(FX_{T_{i-1},T_i}).
benchmark_points.bp17: Assumption (i)(b) implies that mu_{i-1} must be increasing in FX_{T_{i-1},T_i}.
benchmark_points.bp18: In Design A, the drift and FX functional are found jointly by a predictor-corrector scheme.
benchmark_points.bp19: The predictor recovers FX_{T_i} from FX digital call prices.
benchmark_points.bp20: The corrector adjusts the drift to restore arbitrage-freeness.
benchmark_points.bp21: The predictor and corrector steps are iterated until convergence.
benchmark_points.bp23: After mu_{i-1} is frozen, the E_{i,j} are determined.
benchmark_points.bp24: Design A's convergence is only a conjecture.
benchmark_points.bp25: The quoted conjecture is that for a reasonable initial choice of mu_{i-1} the algorithm converges.
benchmark_points.bp26: Design B is described in Markov_Functional_CCY_Model.pdf.
benchmark_points.bp28: In Design B, the drift is derived from no-arbitrage condition (22).
benchmark_points.bp29: In Design B, the exponential form is FX(T_i, y) = exp(ay).
benchmark_points.bp30: For the exponential form, the drift has the analytic form in equation (23).
benchmark_points.bp31: Other functional forms may require solving for mu numerically with a one-dimensional root finder.
benchmark_points.bp32: In Design B, the drift can be derived for the continuous process and then discretised.
benchmark_points.bp33: Deriving the drift for the continuous process and then discretising only guarantees that the discretized model satisfies the no-arbitrage condition up to a discretization error.
benchmark_points.bp34: The preferred route is to derive the drift of the discrete Euler scheme from no-arbitrage.
benchmark_points.bp35: Design A's corrector step is what keeps the model arbitrage-free.
benchmark_points.bp36: Design A's arbitrage-freeness holds only once the iteration has converged.
benchmark_points.bp37: In Design B, with the drift set by (22), the model is arbitrage-free.
benchmark_points.bp38: Under Design B's discrete-scheme route, arbitrage-freeness is exact.
benchmark_points.bp39: Under Design B's continuous-then-discretise route, arbitrage-freeness holds only up to discretisation error.
benchmark_points.bp40: The excerpts do not quantify the residual error of numerical root-finding.
benchmark_points.bp41: Design A allows the Brownian motions W^x, W^y, and W^z to be correlated.
benchmark_points.bp42: Remark 3 on p.8 notes that calibration to foreign caplets is then no longer independent of the other calibrations in general.
benchmark_points.bp43: Calibration to foreign caplets becomes independent again when the increments are independent.
benchmark_points.bp44: Design B assumes zero instantaneous correlation of the driving processes.
benchmark_points.bp45: Non-zero correlation prevents the expectation from decoupling.
benchmark_points.bp47: Non-zero correlation requires a change of numeraire drift for z.
benchmark_points.bp48: Low correlations can be handled by assuming zero correlation over the calibration step only.
benchmark_points.bp49: The base case assumes that rates and FX are instantaneously independent.
benchmark_points.bp50: The base-case assumption that rates and FX are instantaneously independent may be relaxed.
benchmark_points.bp51: Design A fits the FX volatility skew exactly.
benchmark_points.bp52: One risk in Design A lies in the convergence of the predictor-corrector loop.
benchmark_points.bp53: Another risk in Design A is that each step's drift depends on the FX functional being solved for.
benchmark_points.bp54: Design B's fixed exponential form gives a log-normal model.
benchmark_points.bp55: Design B's log-normal model matches only ATM FX options.
benchmark_points.bp56: Freely chosen functional forms at each step allow full smile calibration.
benchmark_points.bp57: A non-analytic drift adds numerical cost.
benchmark_points.bp59: Discretisation error is a source of calibration error on skew-sensitive products.
benchmark_points.bp60: The zero-correlation assumption is a further source of calibration error on skew-sensitive products.
benchmark_points.bp61: If functional forms are recalculated under a changed numeraire, they match the relevant terminal distributions.
benchmark_points.bp62: Recalculated functional forms do not match the transition distributions.
benchmark_points.bp63: Prices of products such as Bermudans may differ as a result.

agent_points.ap1: In cross-currency Markov-functional models, the FX drift is fixed by no-arbitrage.
agent_points.ap2: Once the numeraire pair and the FX functional are chosen, the drift must satisfy the numeraire-relative martingale condition.
agent_points.ap3: Setting the drift to satisfy the numeraire-relative martingale condition makes the model arbitrage-free.
agent_points.ap4: Both designs in the corpus determine the drift from a measure-consistent construction rather than leaving it free.
agent_points.ap5: Determining the drift from a measure-consistent construction permits calibration to FX smiles.
agent_points.ap6: Skew-sensitive hybrids such as PRDC swaps depend on FX skew.
agent_points.ap7: Skew-sensitive hybrids such as PRDC swaps depend on correlation assumptions between FX and rates.
